newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 2.7 pct ahead of votes.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 2.7 pct ahead of votes.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped in selective buys on Tuesday amid positive expectations that votes to take place in parliament this evening would not hurt the government, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed 42 points, or 2.7 percent higher at a day's high of 1,596. Daily volume rose sharply to 27.44 trillion lira from Monday's 18.87 trillion.

Brokers said there was brief selling at the start of the afternoon session due to the resignation of a deputy from the conservative coalition partner True Path Party (DYP) ahead of the votes, but buying resumed quickly afterwards.

"Buying strengthened after sales prompted at the start of the (second) session by the resignation of a deputy from the DYP. The thought that the parliamentary vote results will be positive dominated the market," said Yesim Cambazoglu from Alfa securities.
Parliament began the corruption debate to decide whether to send deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to the Supreme Court on two corruption allegations dating from her three-year term as premier.
Another corruption allegation against Ciller will be debated on Wednesday. All probes were previously rejected by parliamentary commissions, but the general assembly's vote will be final.
Brokers said the market could still remain cautious due to two censure motions filed by leftist parties against the Islamist-led government, scheduled to be taken up in parliament on February 25.
"The parliamentary votes and motions are negatively affecting sentiment. The index is unlikely to pierce the 1,600 resistance even though it tried," said Koray Cervatoglu from Baran securities.
Brokers said the market also lacked excitement after the recent strong rally which carried the index up 74.2 percent from end-1996 to an all-time high closing of 1,700 on January 27.
They said selective purchases were based on 1996 profit prospects of companies.

Of the 238 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 156 to 28 and 54 closed unchanged. The IMKB Industrial jumped 3.03 percent to 1,668, the IMKB Services firmed 0.42 percent to 1,421 and the IMKB Financial gained 3.3 percent to 1,626.

Top actives were car and commercial vehicle producers Tofas Otomobil Fabrikasi, up 1,000 lira at 8,600 and Otosan, up 6,000 lira at 72,000, followed by largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, up 250 lira at 21,000. They made up 17.4 percent of the total turnover.
